subtopic: The Modulus and the Conjugate of a Complex Number
title: Pitfalls & pro-tips: modulus and conjugate

board_content.text: Never write $|z|=\pm z$; the modulus is a single non-negative real.
$\bar z$ flips only the imaginary sign; $-z$ flips both — don't confuse them.
And $z\bar z=|z|^{2}$ is a non-negative real — not $(\bar z)^{2}$ and not $|z|$.
Pro-tip: to prove '$E$ is real', show $E=\bar E$; for 'imaginary', show $E+\bar E=0$.
For moduli of products, powers, and quotients, take $|\cdot|$ factor by factor.
On $|z|=1$, substitute $\bar z=1/z$ — it collapses unit-circle problems.

segments_english.text: Let's finish this subtopic with the traps that reliably cost marks, and the shortcuts that reliably save them.
Biggest trap first: the modulus of a sum is not the sum of the moduli. In general only the less-than-or-equal holds; equality is the exception, not the rule.
Second: never write modulus of z equals plus or minus z. The modulus is one single non-negative real number, full stop.
Third: the conjugate flips only the imaginary sign, while minus z flips both signs. Mixing these two up is one of the most common errors in the chapter.
Fourth: z times z bar is the modulus squared, a non-negative real. It is not z bar squared, and it is not the modulus itself.
Now the pro-tips. To prove an expression E is real, show it equals its own conjugate. To prove it's purely imaginary, show E plus E bar is zero. This usually beats expanding.
For moduli of products, powers, and quotients, always take the modulus factor by factor rather than multiplying everything out.
<whisper>And the unit-circle secret:</whisper> whenever modulus of z is one, replace z bar with one over z. That single substitution collapses a whole class of hard problems.

segments_hinglish.text: Is subtopic ko finish karte hain un traps ke saath jo pakka marks le jaate hain, aur un shortcuts ke saath jo pakka bachate hain.
Sabse bada trap pehle: sum ka modulus, moduli ka sum nahi hai. Generally sirf less-than-or-equal chalta hai; equality exception hai, rule nahi.
Doosra: kabhi modulus of z barabar plus or minus z mat likho. Modulus ek single non-negative real number hai, bas.
Teesra: conjugate sirf imaginary sign flip karta hai, jabki minus z dono signs flip karta hai. In dono ko mix karna chapter ki sabse common errors mein se ek hai.
Chautha: z times z bar hai modulus squared, ek non-negative real. Ye z bar squared nahi hai, aur ye khud modulus bhi nahi hai.

Ab pro-tips. Kisi expression E ko real prove karne ke liye dikhao ki wo apne hi conjugate ke barabar hai. Purely imaginary prove karne ke liye dikhao ki E plus E bar zero hai. Ye aksar expanding se behtar hai.
Products, powers, aur quotients ke moduli ke liye hamesha modulus factor by factor lo, sab kuch multiply karne ke bajaay.
<whisper>Aur unit-circle secret:</whisper> jab bhi modulus of z one ho, z bar ko one over z se replace karo. Wo ek substitution mushkil problems ki poori class collapse kar deti hai.
